title: I Forwarded the Family Inheritance Spreadsheet They Thought Was Private

parts.text: I was added to a sheet titled estate-temp at 10:03 p.m. by accident. It showed my aunt planning to tell me the jewelry was costume while listing the appraisals in a column marked don't tell Nia. I was Nia, thirty-one. I downloaded the sheet. I did not scream. I waited until the next Sunday call. They asked if I wanted the costume box. I asked if they meant the appraised box. Silence like a dropped fork. Then my cousin locked me out of the sheet and sent a text: you weren't supposed to see the formulas.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They locked the sheet and admitted the costume story was a formula.

social.video_title: The estate sheet said don't tell Nia next to the appraisals — Part 1/2
social.description: Accidental access, costume lie, Sunday call. Then a lock. Would you have waited until Sunday?

parts.text: I emailed the executor, who was not my aunt, with the download. Executors like appraisals more than stories. The jewelry went through the will as written, not as costume. My aunt said I had been sneaky. I had been cc'd. I stored the download. I still go to Sunday calls. I do not take costume boxes without numbers. Forks stay on tables. Formulas belong in the open if they divide a life.

social.video_title: The executor preferred appraisals to folklore — Part 2/2
social.description: Will as written, Sunday still happens, no costume fiction. Was a spreadsheet a secret will?
